Sara —

Thanks — great questions. I pulled together answers below and attached a snapshot of our subprocessor roster plus a short operations playbook excerpt. High level: Redwood supports strict region pinning for customer request and also maintains controlled transient processing patterns for availability and caching. Details: 

1) Data types and pinning
- Customer-controlled model input/output (request payloads, generated text) and persisted artifacts (stored records) can be pinned to US/EU/APAC.
- Operational telemetry (agent/daemon metrics), anonymized service metrics, and aggregated telemetry are not covered by region pinning in the standard DPA but we can include additional commitments for particular customers via addendum.

2) Transient cross-region processing policy (operational summary)
- Use cases: cache warm-up after failover, KV-prefix prefetch for hot routes, short-term job routing during capacity bursts, and emergency failover.
- Max windows: default transient window is up to 72 hours for cache/warm-up scenarios; for emergency failover we document and notify customers within 24 hours of event close.
- Controls: transient data is written to ephemeral storage only; KV caches are encrypted at rest with customer-shared keys where requested; KMS usage creates an immutable audit trail.
- Auditing: every transient event is recorded with timestamps, regions touched, and request identifiers; logs are available under our audit export for 90 days and can be extended via contract.

3) Subprocessor visibility
- Attached is the current roster (Subprocessor_Roster_2026-10-18.xlsx). The roster identifies subprocessors that may process data in other regions; we flag those with cross-border activity.

4) Suggested DPA addendum language (2–3 sentences)
- "Redwood Inference will process Customer Data within the region(s) specified in the DPA. Transient cross-region processing (e.g., caching, failover) may occur only for operational reasons and for a maximum continuous period of 72 hours unless otherwise mutually agreed; Redwood will maintain audit logs of any such processing and provide evidence on request within 5 business days."

Next steps: I can loop in our security and legal team to prepare a formal addendum and an evidence package (KMS proof-of-use, sample audit export, signed subprocessor attestations). Would a target of Oct 22 for a draft addendum work for your procurement timeline?

Sara —

Looping in Mina (Security) and Marissa (Legal ops) to respond to the clarifications and produce the sample evidence. Quick answers inline and proposed deliverables/timeline below.

Definitions (proposed addendum glossary) — please tell us if these work for you and your counsel:
- "Transient cross-region processing": short-lived processing of Customer Data outside the pinned region for the sole purpose of availability or operational continuity (examples: KV cache entries created to reduce cold-start latency, prefix cache warm-up, and short failover routing). Does not include batch analytics, model training, or materialized backups.
- "Ephemeral storage": storage that is not replicated to durable backups and is purged within the transient window; ephemeral stores are encrypted and not indexed by long-term search/analytics.

Backups/replication
- Confirmation: We do not place routine backups or durable replication copies of pinned Customer Data outside the selected region. In rare emergency restore scenarios (e.g., disastrous regional outage) temporary replicates may be created outside-region by explicit change-control and we will notify the customer and record the event. That pathway is not used for routine caching or analytics.

Evidence package and timeline (our proposed deliverables)
- By Oct 22: Draft DPA addendum with the glossary and 72-hour window language (Marissa).
- By Oct 22: Sample redacted audit export demonstrating a transient cache warm-up event (Mina). Export will include timestamps, request id, regions touched, and KMS key fingerprint (redacted) — suitable for your DPO to validate logging and key usage.
- By Oct 23: Subprocessor attestation bundle for subprocessors that may conduct cross-border processing (signed CSV/PDF).

If that timeline works we will prepare the artifacts and provide DocuSign-ready addendum language. If you prefer a shorter maximum window (e.g., 24 hours) we can offer that as a negotiated term for customers with stricter residency needs; note that narrower windows may impact availability during cross-region failover scenarios.
